detail.title: Experimental Distinctions Between Autocatalytic Memory and Template-Directed Heredity
detail.summary: This revision formalizes the distinction between irreducible autocatalytic networks, which support persistent history-dependent states via stoichiometric constraints, and template-directed heredity, which requires discrete inheritance mechanisms. Evidence suggests that while autocatalytic persistence provides a substrate for chemical memory, it is distinct from the information-copying fidelity required for Darwinian evolution.
detail.reason: Revision necessary to integrate algebraic criteria for autocatalytic persistence into the heredity transition framework.

Evidence suggests that while autocatalytic persistence provides a substrate for temporal organization, Darwinian evolution necessitates pattern inheritance beyond dissipative non-equilibrium persistence.
detail.reason: Revising notebook to incorporate new evidence on dissipative patterns as a precondition for, but distinct from, heritable information.

children.title: Compositional Heredity and Error Thresholds in Prebiotic Systems

detail.title: Compositional Heredity and Error Thresholds in Prebiotic Systems
detail.summary: This revised analysis synthesizes the algebraic conditions for persistent autocatalytic subnetworks with the thermodynamic requirements for heritable information. Persistence in non-equilibrium reaction networks can be characterized by specific stoichiometric submatrix criteria, providing a structural foundation for units of heredity that precede template-directed replication.
detail.reason: Revision incorporating stoichiometric algebraic conditions into the heredity threshold framework, fulfilling the requirement for upgraded evidence in proj-heredity-thresholds-01.
